This appeal is filed aggrieved by the judgment dated 07.02.2019 in S.C.PCs.No.75 of 2015, passed by the I Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge for Trial of Cases under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Hyderabad, convicting the appellant/accused for the offences under Sections 3 and 7 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act which is punishable under Sections 4 and 8 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and Section 376(2)(i) of IPC and 506 of IPC and sentenced to undergo Rigorous imprisonment for 10 years with a fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of three months for the offence punishable under Section 3 and 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and to undergo rigorous imprisonment for (03) years with a fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default to suffer simple imprisonment for three months for the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act and further sentenced to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- in default to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of 15 days for the offence punishable under Section 506 of I.P.C.

sentences.text: Heard learned Counsel for the appellant and Mr. M.Viveknanda Reddy, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of respondent-State.
3. The case of the prosecution is that appellant/accused who was a poojari, went to the house of P.W.1, father of victim to perform Satyanarayana Pooja.
Again on 23.09.2014, he went to do Pitra Paksha Pooja.
The victim was aged 11 years at that time.
On 03.10.2014, the accused went to the house of P.W.1 to perform Homam and it was completed around 12.30 p.m.
After completing the ritual, the accused asked P.Ws.1 and 2, parents of the victim to go and feed a cow.
P.W.1 along with his wife-P.W.2 went to feed cows near Sai Baba Temple.
Meanwhile, the accused sent the P.W.3/victim girl into the pooja room, he also entered the room, assaulted her and kissed her.
The accused forcibly pressed her breasts.
The victim girl felt pain and requested him not to do so.
Appellant also inserted his two fingers into her private parts.
P.W.3 shouted with pain and the accused caught her hands tightly, closed her mouth and stated that if she discloses the matter to anyone something bad would happen to her parents.
P.Ws.1 and 2 came back and accused went away without making eye contact.
P.W.3 was crying in the room and her parents asked her the reason for weeping.
P.W.3 disclosed to her parents as to what the accused did in their absence.
4. P.W.1, father of the victim lodged English Written complaint to the police on 04.10.2014.
The Police registered the case in Cr.No.424/2014 under Sections 376(2), 506 IPC and Sections 5 r/w 6 and 8 of POCSO Act.
The learned Sessions Judge mainly on the basis of evidence of victim girl convicted the appellant.

sentences.text: The main ground urged by the counsel for the appellant is that the prosecution has failed to prove the age of the victim girl to be less than 12 years.
In the absence of such proof, the offence would not fall under Section 6 but under Section 8 of the POCSO Act.

He further submits that false case has been filed against the appellant/accused as PW.1 was due and amount had to be paid to the appellant for homam and pooja that was performed in the home of P.W.1.
6.
The incident happened on 03.10.2014.
On the next day, complaint was filed narrating specifically regarding the acts of the appellant.
According to the complaint and also the narration given by victim/P.W.3, the appellant forcibly pressed the breast of P.W.3 and also inserted his two fingers into the private parts of P.W.3.
The doctor/P.W.7 examined the victim girl on 04.10.2014 itself.
She noticed bruises over her right breast, left breast, over her left shoulder and on her labia majora.
Her hymen was torn.

7. The version given by victim at the earliest point of time corroborates with the doctor's evidence,
who found bruises on both the breasts and private parts of the victim girl.
8. In so far as the age of the victim, P.W.7/the doctor examined the victim girl and recorded her age as 11 years.

The argument of the learned counsel for the appellant that no birth certificate is filed to prove the age of the victim girl cannot be accepted, keeping in view that the age of the victim girl was stated to be 11 years at the time of the incident and confirmed by the doctor during examination.

9. Under Section 3 of POCSO Act, if the person inserts his fingers into the private parts of the child,
it amounts to penetrative sexual assault.
Section 5 of POCSO Act defines aggravated penetrative sexual assault, if the child less than 12 years is victim of such penetrative sexual assault the minimum punishment is 10 years.
10. In view of the above discussion, there are no grounds in this appeal to interfere with the conviction passed by the learned Sessions Judge and this appeal deserves to be dismissed.
11. Appeal dismissed.
